articles.original_title: AI must be built with Indigenous Knowledges, not against them

A2.title: AI and Indigenous Culture
A2.body:
Australia is celebrating 50 years of NAIDOC Week. This week honors the oldest living culture in the world. Now, people are talking about new technology. They are talking about artificial intelligence, or AI. AI is a new kind of technology. It can do many things. But some people are worried about AI. They think AI can take things from Indigenous people. It can take their knowledge without asking. This is not fair. 
   Indigenous people have a simple principle. It is 'nothing about us, without us.' This means people should not make decisions about them without asking. 
   Australia is trying to be fair. They want to make sure AI is good for everyone. 
   AI can be very helpful. But it can also be bad if it is not used correctly. 
   People need to think about how AI can help Indigenous people. They need to ask them what they think. 
   This is important because Indigenous people have a lot of knowledge. They know many things that can help us. 
   If we work together, we can make AI good for everyone.

B1.title: AI and Indigenous Knowledges
B1.body: Australia is celebrating 50 years of NAIDOC Week. This week honors the world's oldest living culture. However, there is a concern about new technology. Artificial intelligence, or AI, is becoming very powerful. Some people think AI will take Indigenous Knowledges without permission. This has happened with other technologies before. It is like taking something that does not belong to you. The problem is that Indigenous people are not involved in the process. The principle is simple: 'nothing about us, without us.' This means that decisions should not be made about a group of people without their input. Australia wants to make sure that AI is built with Indigenous Knowledges, not against them. This is important because Indigenous people have a lot to offer. They have unique knowledge and perspectives. If AI is built with their help, it can be more fair and respectful. The goal is to make sure that AI benefits everyone, not just a few people. This is a big challenge, but it is also an opportunity. By working together, we can create a better future. The celebration of NAIDOC Week is a reminder of the importance of respecting Indigenous cultures. It is a time to think about how we can work together to build a more inclusive world. This is a chance for Australia to show that it values Indigenous Knowledges and wants to build a better future for everyone.

B2.title: AI and Indigenous Knowledges
B2.body: As Australia celebrates 50 years of NAIDOC Week, it is a time to honor the world's oldest living culture. However, there is a growing concern that artificial intelligence, or AI, may not be developed with the best interests of Indigenous people in mind. The principle of 'nothing about us, without us' is a simple yet important one. It means that any decisions or actions taken should be made with the full participation and consent of the people they affect. Unfortunately, this has not always been the case with new technologies. Many have been used to extract resources and knowledge from Indigenous communities without their consent, credit, or compensation. This has led to a loss of control over their own knowledge and culture. The development of AI is no exception. If AI is built without the input and participation of Indigenous people, it may become another tool that takes their knowledge without giving anything back. This could have serious implications for the preservation and promotion of Indigenous Knowledges. It is essential that AI is developed in a way that respects and values the knowledge and culture of Indigenous people. By working together, we can ensure that AI is used to benefit, rather than harm, these communities. The celebration of NAIDOC Week is a reminder of the importance of respecting and honoring Indigenous cultures. It is a time to reflect on the past and look to the future, to ensure that new technologies like AI are developed in a way that is fair and just for all. This requires a fundamental shift in how we approach the development of AI, one that prioritizes the principles of participation, consent, and reciprocity.

C1.title: AI Development Requires Indigenous Insight
C1.body: As Australia commemorates a significant milestone, marking 50 years of NAIDOC Week, which pays tribute to the world's oldest living culture, a pressing concern has emerged regarding the development and implementation of artificial intelligence. The notion that 'nothing about us, without us' serves as a fundamental principle, underscoring the imperative of incorporating Indigenous Knowledges into the fabric of AI development. The apprehension stems from the fact that AI, much like its technological predecessors, may perpetuate a pattern of exploitation, wherein Indigenous Knowledges are extracted without consent, credit, or reciprocity. This phenomenon is particularly pertinent in the context of Australia's history, where the erosion of Indigenous cultures has been a longstanding issue. The incorporation of Indigenous perspectives into AI development is crucial, as it would not only ensure that the technology is built with, rather than against, Indigenous Knowledges, but also foster a more equitable and inclusive approach to technological advancement. By acknowledging the significance of Indigenous Knowledges and actively seeking to integrate them into AI development, we can mitigate the risk of perpetuating existing power dynamics and work towards a more just and inclusive technological landscape. Ultimately, the success of AI development hinges on its ability to reconcile with the principles of Indigenous Knowledges, thereby ensuring that the technology is developed in a manner that is respectful, responsible, and reciprocal. The celebration of NAIDOC Week serves as a poignant reminder of the importance of prioritizing Indigenous perspectives in all aspects of Australian society, including the development of emerging technologies like AI. The future of AI development in Australia will undoubtedly be shaped by its ability to navigate this complex issue, and it remains to be seen whether the technology will be built in a way that honors and respects Indigenous Knowledges.
